meta.title: Judgment Audit · Judgment diagnostic for implementing AI | A:BRA
meta.description: In one week we audit how one area of your business makes decisions, codify the judgment of the people who decide and deliver a prioritized plan to implement AI where it moves results.

hero.title: Your company is going to implement AI. <muted>The question is where, how and with what judgment.</muted>
hero.lead: In one week we audit how one area of your business makes decisions, codify the judgment of the people who decide and deliver a prioritized plan to implement AI where it actually moves results.
hero.imageAlt: Whale drawn in aqua lines descending into the deep

signals.title: Four signs your decisions <muted>don’t run on a system.</muted>
signals.lead: Before choosing tools you need to know which processes gain from AI, which need data or order first, and which of your company’s rules AI has to respect.

items.title: Blind decisions
items.body: Decisions made on experience or gut feeling, with no data behind them.

items.title: Data that doesn’t decide
items.body: There are reports and dashboards, but they don’t change any decision.

items.title: Routine that drains
items.body: Repetitive decisions with clear rules that a person still makes by hand.

items.title: Judgment in one person
items.body: When that person is out, the process stops.

thesis.lead: Before implementing any tool, you need to understand and codify how your company decides. That layer of judgment is what turns AI into an advantage of your own.

method.title: Five moments. <muted>One condition to move forward in each.</muted>
method.lead: The week starts when we have the complete material, not when the contract is signed. That’s how we protect the promise: a plan in five business days.

phases.name: Prepare
phases.body: Questionnaire, 40 to 60 real cases and read-only access.

phases.name: Expose
phases.body: Interviews and a map of every decision in the area.

phases.name: Codify
phases.body: Workshop with your expert: labeled cases, rules and exceptions.

phases.name: Prioritize
phases.body: Initiatives scored by impact, feasibility and time to value.
phases.gate: Each initiative has a metric and an owner

phases.name: Decide
phases.body: Session with whoever owns the budget.

deliverables.title: Six deliverables that stay with your company, <muted>whether or not you keep working with us.</muted>

items.name: Decision Map
items.what: A map of every decision in the area, sorted into four types.
items.help: See at a glance what’s decided blind, what depends on one person and what can be automated.

items.name: Golden Set
items.what: 20 to 30 real cases labeled with your best expert’s judgment.
items.help: Train and evaluate any AI against your standards, not generic answers.

items.name: Judgment document
items.what: The rules, exceptions and limits your expert decides with, in writing.
items.help: Make sure that knowledge doesn’t depend on one person and can be taught or automated.

items.name: Comparative demo
items.what: AI solving your cases with and without your judgment, with its accuracy rate.
items.help: Measure what codifying your judgment is worth before investing in implementation.

items.name: Judgment Blueprint
items.what: 3 to 5 prioritized initiatives, each with a metric, owner, scope and risks.
items.help: Know what to do first and justify the investment to leadership.

items.name: Next-step proposal
items.what: Three possible paths forward, with scope and timing.
items.help: Decide how to move on with all the information on the table.

example.title: One case, <muted>three answers.</muted>
example.count: 1 of the 20 to 30 cases in the audit
example.question: Should a product piece with the price shown large be approved for an awareness campaign?

answers.why: It follows the brand guidelines: correct colors, logo and typography.
It applies your expert’s rule: in awareness, price doesn’t lead the piece.
The reference answer the AI is measured against.

example.note: In the audit this is repeated with 20 to 30 real cases and we measure the accuracy rate of each version.

areas.title: One method, <muted>four entry points.</muted>
areas.lead: Each area has its own questionnaire, cases and data sources. The method stays the same.

items.name: Sales
items.body: Which lead to prioritize, which discount to approve, when to let an opportunity go.
items.imageAlt: Abstract illustration of light lines converging

items.name: Marketing
items.body: Where to invest, which campaign to scale or cut, how to read attribution.

items.name: Operations
items.body: What to assign to whom, which exception to approve, when to escalate a problem.

items.name: Reputation
items.body: Which mention to answer, when to escalate to a crisis, what to say as a spokesperson.
items.imageAlt: Abstract illustration of the water surface seen from below

projects.title: The method comes from <muted>projects we’ve already built.</muted>

items.name: Longitudinal media monitoring
items.what: Tracks what the media publishes about an organization over time and classifies each mention with AI, using 14 rules that never break and 40 hand-labeled cases.
items.help: The communications team stops reading everything and focuses on the mentions that call for a decision: respond, escalate or let it go.

items.name: Brand value metric
items.what: Net Build Rate, a proprietary metric that measures whether a brand is building or losing value, developed with a global sportswear brand in Mexico.
items.help: Turns brand value into a number you can track over time and defend to leadership, beyond reach and impressions.

items.name: Sales copilot on WhatsApp
items.what: Takes in the leads that arrive on WhatsApp, scores them with AI and suggests a priority and a reply to the salesperson.
items.help: The team serves the highest-potential leads first, and a person always makes the final call before replying.

items.name: DataOps platform with a voice layer
items.what: Connects business data to dashboards and to a voice layer for asking questions in natural language. Licensed to a creative group.
items.help: Leadership checks its indicators whenever it needs them, without waiting for an analyst to build the report.

items.name: AI adoption at a creative agency
items.what: Role-based training with skill templates and a prompt library for content, creative, strategy and operations.
items.help: Each team leaves with tools set up for its daily work, not general theory about AI.

items.name: AI training for mass transit
items.what: A 10-session, 20-hour program for the teams of a transit company.
items.help: Designed so each team decides which tasks to delegate to AI and how to validate what it produces.

items.name: Execute with A:BRA

items.label: Path B
items.name: Execute with your team

items.label: Path C

meta.title: A:BRA — Strategy, development and data with applied AI
meta.description: Strategy, development and data with applied AI. A hybrid growth and engineering studio: what we recommend, we first validate in our own products.

hero.title: We build growth systems. <muted>And the products that make them possible.</muted>
hero.lead: Strategy, development and data with applied AI, for companies that want to grow with judgment, not intuition.

problem.title: The problem isn't a lack of data. <muted>It's that marketing, product and technology work as islands.</muted>
problem.body: You invest in ads, hire agencies, install dashboards. And you still feel like you're operating blind. The reason is structural: your brand, your website, your product and your ads were built at different times, by different vendors, with no system to coordinate them.

signals.title: A brand that doesn't scale
signals.body: Your message changes with every campaign. Sales says one thing, the website another, the ads another.

signals.title: Ads that burn money
signals.body: High volume, low quality, unclear attribution. CAC goes up and nobody knows why.

signals.title: Technology that slows you down
signals.body: Your stack is a collection of tools, not a system. Every new integration breaks something.

signals.title: AI that answers generically
signals.body: You use AI, but the results look like any other company's. It lacks your business's judgment.

services.title: Four capabilities. <muted>One integrated system.</muted>
services.lead: Each capability works on its own, but performs better connected: strategy defines what to measure, data shows what works and development turns it into a system.

items.title: Strategy
items.body: We decide what to say, to whom and how to grow, with data instead of intuition.

items.title: Development
items.body: We build the pieces that make the system work, fast and without breaking.

items.title: Data & AI
items.body: We turn data into decisions: what to measure, how to read it and what to automate.

items.title: Growth
items.body: We take the system to market and improve it every cycle.
includes: Content and social media, with MTM

method.title: A:BRA Loop. <muted>The system where growth and engineering feed each other.</muted>
method.lead: Most agencies sell strategy. Product studios sell code. We operate at the intersection: every marketing decision is validated by building, and every product is built with growth logic from day one.

phases.name: Insight
phases.title: Diagnosis with judgment
phases.body: We understand how your business decides before recommending tools. It can start with a one-week Judgment Audit.

phases.name: Build
phases.title: Growth systems
phases.body: Brand, website, landing pages, automations and digital products, prototyped with AI and built with technical rigor.

phases.name: Launch
phases.title: Integrated launch
phases.body: Ads, SEO and content, with predictive models to segment, bid and attribute.

phases.name: Learn
phases.title: Analytics and iteration
phases.body: Dashboards and continuous iteration. Learning flows back into Insight, and the system improves with every cycle.

method.quote: It's not a funnel. It's a flywheel: every turn of the Loop increases knowledge, lowers cost and accelerates growth.

process.title: From diagnosis to a running system. <muted>In 30 days.</muted>

steps.body: Judgment Audit: the area's decisions, data and priorities.
Pillars, KPIs and the technical architecture for growth.
Campaigns, website, automations and AI models up and running.
Data-driven iteration and a closing executive report.

founder.title: Gerardo Riarte. <muted>Growth, AI and product in one profile.</muted>
founder.body: A:BRA was born from a simple idea: marketing works better when the person who designs the strategy also knows how to build. I'm Argentinian and live in Bogotá. I've spent more than a decade designing growth strategies for brands in Latin America, developing digital products and applying AI to business decisions. That combination is what I bring to every project: understand the problem, decide with data and build the solution.

lab.title: We build our own products. <muted>That's how we know what works.</muted>
lab.lead: Most agencies sell strategies they never executed with their own money. We validate the A:BRA Loop on real products before applying it to clients.
lab.microcopy: Nougram was born in our lab to solve a concrete market pain: pricing knowledge work with predictable net profit.

highlights: Lock in your net profit before signing each proposal.
Leave the math to AI and refocus on creating value.
Built for consultants, designers, marketers and agencies.
